Shorting The Grid

by Meredith Angwin
Shorting the Grid, The Hidden Fragility of Our Electric Grid is an exposé of the insider-ruled practices of the “deregulated” areas of the United States electric grid. The grid in these areas is managed by a regional transmission organization (RTO). Within these organizations, no group is responsible or accountable for grid reliability. The RTO areas have higher retail electricity prices, no way for ordinary citizens to influence decisions, and a more fragile grid. Using the rules and history of the New England grid as an example, the book shows how RTO areas are moving steadily to a future of “rolling blackouts” where the grid operator deliberately cuts power to one section of the grid after another.

Meredith knows the grid with years of experience both as a very active ratepayer and direct involvement in some of the bodies that make up the complex policy grid.
She has written the book Shorting the Grid: The Hidden Fragility of Our Electric Grid which I highly recommend. Her discussion of the Policy Grid and how that adds significantly to the fragility of our grid should be read by anyone concerned about reliable power.
She also has a substack The Electric Grandma (love the name) where she provides updates to what she sees coming on the grid. Well worth following.
In this interview we discuss four questions:
1. What has changed since she wrote her book.
2. What she thinks needs to change on the grid.
3. What she thinks will change on the grid.
4. Should we all get solar + batteries at home, out of pure self interest?
